title: Provider overclaims delivered hours
theme: Could a provider claim for more training than it delivered, and does that need anyone else's cooperation?

messages.text: Simulated: class time is shortened; the course record is unchanged.

contributions.description: Records more training hours than were delivered.

grounding.relation: S2 questions price relative to content, consistent with less being delivered than paid for.

contributions.description: Claims funding for the recorded hours.

flows.description: Funding for hours recorded but not delivered.

assumptions.text: Trainees do not see or sign the hour-level delivery record.

messages.text: Simulated: unaware of what is recorded; no action taken.

source_findings.note: Price complaint only; consistent with but not indicative of overclaiming.

assumption_findings.note: Test whether trainees attest at session level.

review.mo_rationale: Matches MO-07, claims exceeding training delivered. MO-07 basis is observed overseas, so local applicability is an assumption.

test_data_needed.data_item: Claimed hours versus scheduled session hours per course run

test_data_needed.purpose: Compare actual session length with recorded length

concerns: Single-actor misconduct: route to standard provider audit rather than collusion review.
